correctness.rationale: Reconstructed exact distances: point-point 2, incident point-line 1/nonincident 3, intersecting lines 2/parallel lines 4. Every mixed scale-two clique lies in a line cone over its incident points or a point cone over its incident lines because two points share exactly one line. U (point simplex plus line cones) collapses to the point simplex; V (nonparallel-line flag complex plus point cones) collapses to B, the join of q+1 discrete q-element parallel classes. Their exact intersection is the original incidence graph G. Homotopy pushout and simply connected B yield B wedge suspension(G); B has (q-1)^(q+1) q-spheres and G cyclerank (q-1)^2(q+1). The scale-3 point apex is universal. This proves arbitrary existing affine planes including non-Desarguesian ones; the independent Hesse q=3 incidence count (21 vertices,36 edges,16 cycles) and package finite GF(2) Rips verifier only corroborate, not replace the symbolic all-order proof.
correctness.risk: All-order argument uses finite affine plane axioms and simplicial cofibrations; it does not assert anything about weighted metrics or arbitrary partial linear spaces.

final_claim: For any existing finite affine plane of order \(q\ge3\), the inclusive unit-edge graph-metric scale-two Rips complex of its point-line incidence graph is \(\bigvee^{(q-1)^2(q+1)}S^2\vee\bigvee^{(q-1)^{q+1}}S^q\); its scale-one Rips complex has \((q-1)^2(q+1)\) circles and every scale \(\ge3\) is contractible, with the asserted positive-dimensional persistence intervals over every field.
limitations: Only finite affine planes that exist, with q>=3; no existence claim for arbitrary integers.
Unit-edge graph shortest-path and inclusive Rips thresholds; all positive-dimensional bars only.
